page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.metal-48xl is a bare-metal instance designed for high-concurrency general-purpose workloads requiring direct access to underlying physical hardware. The system is driven by Intel x86_64 processors delivering 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs clocked at 3.9 GHz with two threads per core. Because CPU allocation is dedicated and bypasses a hypervisor layer, workloads run without virtualization overhead or noisy-neighbor interference.

The memory footprint totals 768 GB, offering an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture features 11,400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage directly mounted to the machine, supporting high-throughput disk I/O. Network performance is anchored by a 200 Gbps baseline bandwidth, providing substantial capacity for inter-node communication and heavy network traffic.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the dense packaging of 192 vCPUs, 768 GB RAM, and over 11 TB of local NVMe storage enables significant workload consolidation. Relying on local NVMe disks can minimize external block storage usage for temporary files and high-throughput scratch data. The principal architectural tradeoff involves the ephemeral nature of direct instance store volumes, which require deliberate replication strategies to preserve critical data across machine rebuilds.

Given its balanced memory density, high clock speed, low-latency bare-metal access, and sizable local storage capacity, the m8idb.metal-48xl is configured for large relational database engines, high-speed transactional analytics, distributed caching tiers, and intensive batch processing systems.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idb.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server delivering dedicated access to 96 physical Intel cores and 192 vCPUs operating at 3.9 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it integrates 768 GB of system memory alongside 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, completely eliminating hypervisor virtualization overhead. The platform provides a 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating high-throughput data ingestion, rapid inter-node communication, and distributed workloads without supplemental GPU acceleration. Its standard 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU ratio pairs with extensive local scratch disk capacity to deliver strong resource density for consolidating enterprise compute fleets. The primary tradeoff centers on the ephemeral nature of local instance storage, requiring robust external replication for persistent datasets. This configuration is well matched for high-concurrency relational databases, real-time transactional analytics, distributed ETL processing, and large-scale enterprise application hosting.
